what_happened: The job "check declared build inputs against compiled-in files" (a retry, gznq) ended failed before any work was judged. The producer's call was refused with a 401 because its OAuth access token had expired. This was an environment failure. No acceptance criterion was judged and no check failed.
cause: Athena treats the agent login as always valid. It does not check credential validity or expiry before dispatching a producer, and it does not refresh the token. A lapsed token therefore surfaces only as a mid-job 401, which spends a job attempt and a retry on an environment fault that a preflight could have caught. Because of this, a retry can fail for the same reason as the earlier attempt.
prevention: Add a credential preflight before every agent stage and before each retry. It makes a cheap authenticated call or reads the token expiry. If the token is expired or close to expiry, it refreshes it automatically. If it cannot refresh, it holds the job as "waiting for login", with a clear message, and does not run or fail the job. A 401 from an agent should be classed as an environment stop, so it neither consumes the job's attempt or budget nor counts as a job failure. The held job should resume once the the person running Athena re-authenticates.
proposed_request: Add an agent credential preflight to Athena. Before dispatching any agent stage (reader, planner, critic, producer, verifier) and before each retry, Athena checks that the agent's OAuth token is valid and not about to expire. If it can refresh the token, it does so. If not, it holds the job in a visible "waiting for login" state with a message telling whoever runs Athena to re-authenticate. A job held this way is not marked failed, its attempt and budget are not spent, and it resumes on the next drain after re-authentication. A 401 "token has expired" response arriving mid-stage is classed as an environment stop with the same hold behavior, not as a job failure. Acceptance: (1) a test with a fake expired credential shows the job is held, not failed, and that no producer run is started; (2) a test with a mid-stage 401 shows the job ends in the hold state with its attempt count unchanged; (3) after the credential is replaced, the held job resumes and runs; (4) the existing tests pass. Then re-queue the job "check declared build inputs against compiled-in files" (the retry of job 20261102-205414-9c2g) once this lands.
